scope: Current factual package for the members Construction contract activity. It proposes integration records only: no route order, contract count, XP rate, travel time, material stock, points, reward ownership, or player readiness is asserted.

included: Access, contractors, locations, contract tiers, boost boundary, required materials and reusable tools, contract lifecycle, deterministic reward tables, reward-shop stock, permanent utility, repeatability, attention boundary, and account observations.
Exact material and XP formula components are recorded, while contract layout, actual furniture, consumed quantities, game-awarded XP, and points remain reported per contract.
excluded: A final Ironman route, preferred contract tier, expected contracts, XP/hour, contracts/hour, travel time, plank cost, collection-log completion plan, player-owned materials, teleports, points, rewards, or readiness.
Community route, plank sourcing, reward-order, and stopping advice is retained only as strategy-candidate-not-fact.

source_catalog.use: Primary current source for membership/POH access, contractors, cities, tiers, materials, tools, boost boundary, furniture process, tea, contract completion, reward points, shop stock, and collection-log context.
Current contract-layout model, per-tier material/XP ranges and averages, repair/build XP components, and randomness boundary. Crowd-derived averages are not treated as a player's output.
Carpenter outfit total Construction XP effect and wieldable-tool context.
Official launch context and original activity design; superseded values are not preferred over current Wiki mechanics.
Official quality-of-life update context for same-tier contractor assignment and tea interaction improvements.

source_catalog.publisher: Old School RuneScape Wiki community guide
source_catalog.use: Ironman-oriented travel, plank sourcing, and reward-order claims; strategy context only.
Historical community experience report; strategy context only, never a rate or resource fact.
Community client implementation for visible contract-state assistance; not an authority for player observations or game-rule values.

requirements.player_owned_house: A player-owned house is required to participate.
requirements.boost_boundary: Visible temporary Construction boosts can select a contract tier. Invisible boosts such as the crystal saw cannot select a tier. Furniture build requirements are separately boostable, including crystal-saw assistance; a contract cannot be cancelled, so a selected boosted tier must not imply future readiness.

location_and_transport: Amy is the initial contractor and company head in Falador, south of the park.
After the first assignment, Marlo in Varrock, Ellie in East Ardougne, and Angelo in Hosidius can also issue contracts. Each office is in or near that city's estate-agent area.
A contract can assign East Ardougne, south-east Falador, north-east or south Varrock, or south/central Hosidius, including the issuer's current city.

Teleport, spellbook, charge, house-location, and route availability are account observations. NPC Contact is a possible remote contractor-contact capability only when its separate quest, Magic, spellbook, rune, and accessibility requirements are observed.

unlock_transition.from: No player-owned-house or no observed Mahogany Homes first assignment
unlock_transition.to: Player-owned house present and first contract assignment observed
unlock_transition.determinism: Speaking to Amy produces the first contract when the access requirements are actually met; the resulting city, homeowner, layout, and required repairs/builds are not predetermined.

entry_inputs.requirement: Observed tier selection meeting its current/qualifying boosted Construction requirement. The assigned home and layout are randomised from fixed possibilities.

The selected tier's plank type is consumed by the assigned build/repair hotspots. A repair can also consume a steel bar. Exact furniture, material type, and quantity are contract-layout observations; nails are not required.
A hammer and saw are required. A normal hammer/saw, wieldable alternatives, or a one-slot Amy's saw setup must be observed rather than assumed.

entry_inputs.consumed: Any teleport charges, tablets, runes, coins, or other traversal inputs are route-dependent and are only consumed after a reported use.
entry_inputs.requirement: Reach the assigned client's house and later a contractor or separately available NPC Contact route.

reusable_setup.detail: The contract remains assigned until completed; it cannot be cancelled. A completed contract can be followed by another assignment.
Hammer, saw, Amy's saw, plank sack, rune pouch, spellbook, teleports, and Carpenter outfit are reusable-state observations. They do not create materials, contact capabilities, charges, or readiness.

contract_assignment_and_work.assignment: Speak to Amy for the first contract; thereafter speak to an office contractor or use a separately observed eligible NPC Contact capability. The player selects an eligible tier. The client/location and one of the client's fixed layouts are assigned randomly.
contract_assignment_and_work.furniture_loop: At the home, complete every marked repair or build. Broken repair furniture requires one selected-tier plank or one steel bar according to the assigned object; build hotspots consume the selected tier's plank quantity. Completion is blocked until all assigned work is done.
contract_assignment_and_work.tea_and_completion: Speak to the homeowner after all assigned furniture is complete. The completed contract awards its tier completion XP and Carpenter points; the homeowner offers tea that restores run energy to 100% when accepted. Tea use, current energy, accepted/declined state, and all game-awarded values are observations.

xp_components.formula_boundary: Total contract XP is the sum of observed build/repair events plus the selected tier's completion XP, then only documented applicable equipment bonuses. It is never estimated from a planned tier, average layout, elapsed time, or community rate.

completion_or_reward_events.condition: Observed assigned contract, all its marked furniture completed, and homeowner spoken to.

deterministic_effects_given_observed_tie.tea: A homeowner tea offer can restore run energy to 100% if accepted.

completion_or_reward_events.condition: Observed Carpenter-point balance is sufficient and the specific Reward Shop purchase is confirmed.
completion_or_reward_events.boundary: A purchase creates the particular deterministic reward/unlock. Supply crate contents, collection-log entry completion, later use, and player readiness remain observed.

failure_and_death.failure: There is no cancellation path for an assigned contract. Missing tools/materials, unreachable location, or insufficient level for an assigned build blocks progress until the player actually resolves it.
failure_and_death.death: Mahogany Homes itself is a non-combat city activity. Any death, dangerous travel, item loss, reclaim, or teleport interruption comes from an externally chosen route and must be handled by that route's state model.
failure_and_death.logout_and_interruption: This package does not infer persistence or loss from an unobserved logout/disconnection. Reported assignment/work state must be reconciled against actual game state before effects are recorded.

repeatability.cycle: After an observed completed contract, obtain another tier-selected assignment from an available contractor or separately observed NPC Contact route. Each assignment has independent random city/client/layout and independently observed material, XP, point, and travel outcomes.
repeatability.rng_boundary: The assignment and fixed layout selection are random. Supply crates have contents not fixed by their purchase price. Neither creates a guaranteed material, output, or time result.

currencies.spend_behavior: A completed observed contract adds 2/3/4/5 points for Beginner/Novice/Adept/Expert. Reward-shop costs are fixed; current balance and purchase readiness are observed only.

Planks and occasional steel bars are per-layout consumed inputs; logs, sawmill fees, spell materials, teleport inputs, and travel source selection are separate dependencies. No material or coin balance is inferred.

utility: Construction XP from observed work and completion
Carpenter-point currency for deterministic shop purchases
rewards.boundary: Actual contract work, materials, XP, points, and balance must be reported or independently game-verified.

utility: Reusable carrying-capacity utility; contents and ownership are observed.
Can be swapped to off-hand; it does not provide the crystal saw's invisible Construction boost.
Each owned and worn piece gives its documented Construction XP bonus
Full worn outfit totals 2.5% Construction XP bonus.
rewards.boundary: Piece ownership and worn state are separate observations; no full-set ownership or XP bonus is inferred.

utility: Unlocks the Hosidius Wall Kit for the player-owned house.

rewards.boundary: The purchase is deterministic but crate contents are not. No planks, bars, nails, coins, or other contents are inferred until opened and reported.

dependencies_and_bypasses.detail: The selected contract tier requires regular/oak/teak/mahogany planks; exact assigned consumption depends on observed layout.
Some repair assignments require a steel bar; exact need is observed per layout.
Deterministic plank conversion paths can supply input planks once their own logs, GP/runes, quest, skill, and location requirements are observed.
Its independent reward pool can produce regular/oak planks; result contents remain RNG observations and are not a planned supply quantity.
350 Carpenter-point deterministic shop purchase, subject to observed balance and confirmed purchase.
500 Carpenter-point deterministic shop purchase, subject to observed balance and confirmed purchase.
Four deterministic shop purchases totaling 2,000 Carpenter points, subject to observed balance and purchases.
2,000 Carpenter-point blueprints purchase, subject to observed balance and confirmed purchase.

logout_or_idle_constraints: Contracts require active navigation, client-house interaction, furniture repair/build actions, and completion dialogue.
No reliable AFK duration, contract rate, or travel time is modeled because these depend on assignment, route, input setup, execution, and external state.
afk_and_attention.source_boundary: Current Wiki describes a travel-and-interaction contract loop; neither it nor community rate guides authorize a predicted attention interval or output rate for this account.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Community guides commonly prioritize plank sack, then Amy's saw, then Carpenter outfit for continued Mahogany Homes training.

Community setups combine city teleports, a Hosidius access method, and NPC Contact to reduce contractor/travel downtime; exact viability depends on separately observed quests, Magic, runes, charges, house setup, and location state.

Community Ironman guidance compares forestry, Kingdom, PvM/reward sources, sawmills, and Plank Make for plank acquisition; these are alternative dependency paths, not assumed stock or a preferred route.

state_boundaries: Do not infer a player-owned house, membership state, Construction level, visible boost, tool, plank sack, Amy's saw, Carpenter outfit, plank count/type, steel-bar count, coins, logs, sawmill access, spellbook, NPC Contact, runes, teleport, charge, house location, contractor access, contract assignment, client, layout, furniture state, tea result, XP, Carpenter points, reward purchase, supply-crate contents, collection-log state, or readiness.

The tier's point award and completion XP are deterministic only after the completed tier is observed. Build/repair XP and consumption are calculated only from observed hotspot events, never from a per-tier average.
Community cost, rate, plank-per-hour, contracts-per-hour, stop, and reward-order claims are strategy candidates only.

conflicts_and_unknowns.conflict: The current mechanics page publishes crowd-derived per-tier layout averages and community guides publish cost/rate estimates, while individual assignments have random client/layout and observed travel/execution.
conflicts_and_unknowns.resolution: Use exact point and completion-XP awards by observed tier plus actual recorded hotspot events. Retain averages only as sourced context; never transition predicted plank/bar use, XP, time, or points from them.

conflicts_and_unknowns.conflict: The current Wiki labels a common experience-efficient purchase order and community guides recommend tier/reward targets, but these depend on current account goals, materials, travel, and owned capability.
conflicts_and_unknowns.resolution: Preserve as strategy-candidate-not-fact. The only normalized deterministic claim is each shop item's current point cost and stated utility after a confirmed purchase.

conflicts_and_unknowns.conflict: Guides describe rapid contractor/travel setups without proving this account's Lunar quest completion, Magic level, spellbook, runes, rune pouch, charged items, POH facilities, or city-route availability.
conflicts_and_unknowns.resolution: Model NPC Contact and transports as independent observed capabilities. Do not use guide routes to imply travel time or contract throughput.

conflicts_and_unknowns.conflict: The shop purchase is fixed at 25 points, but contents are a container outcome rather than a fixed material grant.
conflicts_and_unknowns.resolution: Normalize the purchasable crate and mark its contents as player-observed/RNG. No crate-derived plank, bar, nail, coin, or resource transition is emitted automatically.
